summary: npm package ships obfuscated PowerShell reflective.NET loader as its sole payload
details: serpacksven@1.0.2 ships only four files: package.json and three identical PowerShell scripts disguised with document-like names (client.doc, json.txt, json.txt.1). The PowerShell scripts hide the console window via a ShowWindow(hWnd,0) P/Invoke, base64-decode a large embedded blob, XOR-decrypt it with a hardcoded key to produce a.NET assembly, and reflectively load and invoke the assembly's entry point via Assembly.Load / GetMethod(...).Invoke(). The scripts use heavy junk-variable padding typical of staged PowerShell malware. package.json declares main: index.js but no index.js is present in the tarball, so the package has no library function and no npm lifecycle hooks; its sole shipped content is a Windows reflective-loader dropper intended to be executed by a separate component that fetches or references these files.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
